title: Teams meeting policy: which meeting features does each user get?
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the meeting policy controls, assignment precedence and feature-specific licensing statements. The distinction between an organiser turning Copilot off and a policy setting an overridable Off default is correctly stated.

claims.claim: A meeting policy is a set of settings controlling the meeting features available to organisers and participants.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can use meeting and events policies to control the features that are available to organizers and participants of meetings and events in your organization.

claims.claim: Meeting policies can be managed in the Teams admin centre.
claims.quote: Depending on the feature, you can manage meeting policies in the Microsoft Teams admin center or through PowerShell.

claims.claim: Meeting policies can be managed with the Teams PowerShell module.
claims.quote:
MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module
The Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet allows administrators to update existing meeting policies that can be assigned to particular users to control Teams features related to meetings.

claims.claim: Each user has one effective meeting policy.
claims.quote: A user has one effective policy for each policy type.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: The Global policy applies where there is neither a direct custom assignment nor an applicable group assignment.
claims.quote: If a user isn't a member of any groups that are assigned a policy, the global (Org-wide default) policy for that policy type applies to the user.

claims.claim: Administrators can edit the Global meeting policy.
claims.quote: You can edit the global policy and any custom policies that you create.

claims.claim: Administrators can create named custom meeting policies.
claims.quote: You can edit the settings in the global policy or create and assign one or more custom policies.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can be assigned only one meeting policy and one events policy at a time.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Meeting policy is not events policy
claims.claim: Events have recording settings in a separate events policy.
claims.quote: Meetings and events each have their own recording policies that you can manage.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Meeting policy is not events policy
claims.claim: Events have transcription settings in events policies.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies.
Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.

claims.where: What it is: Who a setting applies to
claims.claim: Microsoft describes three implementation types: per-organiser, per-user, and their combination.
claims.quote:
Policies are implemented in one of the following ways:
Per-organizer
Per-user
Per-organizer and per-user

claims.where: What it is: implementation table; Why it matters
claims.claim: For a per-organiser policy, participants inherit the organiser's policy.
claims.quote: When you implement a per-organizer policy, all participants inherit the policy of the organizer.

claims.claim: Who can bypass the lobby is Microsoft's example of a per-organiser policy.
claims.quote: For example, Who can bypass the lobby is a per-organizer policy

claims.claim: A per-user policy allows or prevents a feature for each user.
claims.quote: When you implement a per-user policy, the policy allows or prevents a given feature for each user.

claims.claim: Meet now in channel meetings is Microsoft's example of a per-user policy.
claims.quote: For example, Meet now in channel meetings is a per-user policy.

claims.claim: The combined implementation restricts participants based on their own policy and the organiser's policy.
claims.quote: When you implement a combination of a per-organizer and per-user policy, certain features are restricted for participants based on their policy and the organizer's policy.

claims.where: What it is: implementation table; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Meeting recording is a per-organiser and per-user policy.
claims.quote: For example, Meeting recording is a per-organizer and per-user policy.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets; controls[2].note; What to check
claims.claim: A directly assigned policy takes precedence over group and Global policies.
claims.quote: If a user is directly assigned a policy (either individually or through a batch assignment), that policy takes precedence.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets; Governance controls
claims.claim: Without a direct assignment, the highest-ranked applicable group assignment determines the policy.
claims.quote: the user inherits the policy of the group assignment that has the highest ranking.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets
claims.claim: Rank 1 is the highest group assignment ranking.
claims.quote: Smaller the number, the higher the ranking with 1 being the highest ranking.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets
claims.claim: Policies can be assigned individually, in batches, or through groups.
claims.quote: Assign a policy directly to users, either individually or at scale through a batch assignment, or to a group that the users are members of.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy a user gets
claims.claim: Policy assignments can be made in the Teams admin centre.
claims.quote: You can make and view assignments in the Teams admin center.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: Changing Global affects users who have no custom policy assignment.
claims.quote: To apply changes to all users in your organization who don't have an existing policy assignment, use the Global policy.

claims.claim: The organiser needs recording permission for a meeting to be recorded.
claims.quote: Both the organizer and recording initiator need to have recording permissions to record the meeting or event.

claims.claim: The person starting a recording also needs recording permission.
claims.quote: Both the organizer and recording initiator need to have recording permissions to record the meeting or event.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Transcription needs two parties; controls[4].note
claims.claim: The organiser's transcription policy must be on for their meeting to include a transcript.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: The user starting the recording or transcript must also have transcription enabled.
claims.quote: The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: The meeting policy overview and assignment pages state no licence for meeting policies themselves.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting policy licensing meeting policies themselves price meter. Read meeting-policies-overview, policy-assignment-overview and assign-policies-users-and-groups on learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams; none states a licence for policies themselves.

claims.claim: Those overview and assignment pages state no meter for meeting policies themselves.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting policy licensing meeting policies themselves price meter. Read meeting-policies-overview, policy-assignment-overview and assign-policies-users-and-groups on learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams; none states a meter for policies themselves.

claims.claim: Copilot in Teams meetings lists an add-on Microsoft Copilot licence for intended users as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: An add-on Microsoft Copilot license for intended users.

claims.claim: Live translated transcription requires the meeting organiser to have Teams Premium.
claims.quote: The meeting or event organizer must have a Teams Premium license for attendees to use live translated transcription.

claims.claim: Live translated captions in meetings require the organiser to have Teams Premium.
claims.quote: The meeting or event organizer must have a Teams Premium license for attendees to use live translated captions.

claims.claim: Teams Premium organisers can use meeting options to control who can record and transcribe.
claims.quote: Organizers with a Teams Premium license can use their meeting options to control who can record and transcribe.

claims.claim: Meeting recordings are stored in the organiser's OneDrive or SharePoint storage.
claims.quote: It gets uploaded to the meeting organizer's OneDrive (private meetings) or SharePoint (channel meetings).

claims.claim: Transcripts are stored with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint.
claims.quote: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risks and limits: Allowing recording does not provide storage
claims.claim: AllowCloudRecording does not configure or validate recording storage.
claims.quote: -AllowCloudRecording controls whether users can record meetings; it doesn't configure or validate recording storage.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A direct assignment silently beats a group assignment
claims.claim: A direct assignment must be removed before the user inherits a group policy of the same type.
claims.quote: you have to remove that policy from the user before they can inherit a policy of the same type from a group.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A direct assignment silently beats a group assignment
claims.claim: Microsoft documents bulk unassignment as a way to remove direct assignments.
claims.quote: When you unassign policies in bulk, you're removing policy assignments that were assigned to individual users through direct assignment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps; controls[1].note; What to check
claims.claim: Group assignments propagate only to direct members, not nested group members.
claims.quote: Group policy assignments are only propagated to users who are direct members of the group. The assignments aren't propagated to members of nested groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps; What to check
claims.claim: Groups with HiddenGroupMembership enabled cannot use group policy assignment.
claims.quote: Groups with the HiddenGroupMembership setting enabled can't use group policy assignment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps
claims.claim: Class Teams have HiddenGroupMembership enabled by default.
claims.quote: Class Teams have this setting enabled by default.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps
claims.claim: Propagation of a group assignment to its members is a background operation.
claims.quote: the propagation of the policy assignment to members of the group is performed as a background operation and might take some time, depending on the size of the group.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps; Open questions
claims.claim: The group assignment article gives no group-size-specific propagation time.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting policies licensing meter group policy propagation time large groups. Read learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/assign-policies-users-and-groups in full; it says propagation might take some time depending on group size, without a size-specific duration.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group assignment has gaps; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft's general Teams policy guidance says changes may take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: Policies are managed through the Teams Admin Center or the Teams PowerShell module, and changes may take up to 24 hours to take effect.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Policies cannot be tidied freely
claims.claim: A policy cannot be deleted while users are assigned to it.
claims.quote: You can't delete a policy if users are assigned to it. You must first assign a different policy to all affected users, and then you can delete the original policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Policies cannot be tidied freely
claims.claim: A policy's name cannot be changed after creation.
claims.quote: After you create a policy, its name can't be changed.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An organiser turning Copilot off; What to check
claims.claim: An organiser turning Copilot off in meeting or event options also turns recording off.
claims.quote: When organizers turn off Copilot for their meeting or event, recording and transcription are also turned off.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An organiser turning Copilot off; What to check
claims.claim: An organiser turning Copilot off in meeting or event options also turns transcription off.
claims.quote: When organizers turn off Copilot for their meeting or event, recording and transcription are also turned off.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An organiser turning Copilot off; What to check
claims.claim: The policy's Copilot Off value sets the organiser's default meeting option to Off.
claims.quote: When organizers with this policy create meetings and events, Copilot's default value in their meeting options is Off.

claims.where: Risks and limits: An organiser turning Copilot off; What to check
claims.claim: Organisers can override the policy's Copilot Off default.
claims.quote: Organizers can change this value to Only during the meeting or During and after the meeting.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Allowing recording does not provide storage
claims.claim: A recording that cannot upload to OneDrive or SharePoint is held in temporary storage.
claims.quote: If a recording can't be uploaded to OneDrive or SharePoint, it's temporarily stored in async media storage

claims.where: Risks and limits: Allowing recording does not provide storage
claims.claim: The temporarily stored recording must be downloaded within 21 days or it is deleted.
claims.quote: must be downloaded within 21 days. Otherwise, the recording is deleted.

claims.claim: External participants cannot record meetings except through third-party compliance recording.
claims.quote: External participants can't record meetings except when it's a Teams third-party compliance recording.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Meeting policy is not events policy; controls[6].governs
claims.claim: The meeting policy's Copilot setting also governs the default Copilot option for events.
claims.quote: When organizers with this policy create meetings and events, Copilot's default value in their meeting options is Only during the meeting.

claims.claim: Teams Administrator can manage meeting policies.
claims.quote:
Teams Administrator
Manage meetings, including meeting policies, configurations, and conference bridges.

claims.claim: Teams Communications Administrator can manage meeting policies.
claims.quote:
Teams Communications Administrator
Manage meetings, including meeting policies, configurations, and conference bridges.

claims.claim: Teams Reader has read-only access to meeting policy settings.
claims.quote: Read everything in the Teams admin center, but not update anything

claims.claim: These administrator roles are assigned through Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: You can assign users or groups to these roles in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: An assignment without a specified ranking receives the lowest ranking.
claims.quote: If you don't specify a ranking, the policy assignment is given the lowest ranking.

claims.claim: Changing a group assignment's ranking in the admin centre requires removing and re-adding the assignment.
claims.quote: To change the ranking of a group assignment, you need to remove the group policy assignment first. Then, follow the steps above to assign the policy to a group.

claims.claim: PowerShell Grant cmdlets can change an existing group assignment's ranking.
claims.quote:
After you assign a policy to a group, you can use the appropriate Grant cmdlet to change that group's policy assignment as follows:
- Change the ranking

claims.claim: Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy lists meeting policies configured in the organisation.
claims.quote: Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy is called without any additional parameters; this returns a collection of all the teams meeting policies configured for use in your organization.

claims.claim: Transcription is on by default for new meeting policies.
claims.quote: Toggle Transcription On or Off. This setting is On by default for new policies.

claims.claim: Live captions is a per-user policy.
claims.quote: This setting is a per-user policy and applies during a meeting.

claims.claim: DisabledUserOverride permits users to turn on live captions.
claims.quote:
DisabledUserOverride
Live captions are off by default, but users with this assigned policy can turn on live captions during meetings or events.

claims.quote:
On with saved transcript required | EnabledWithTranscript

claims.claim: The cited pages do not name audit events for changes to meeting policy settings.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "meeting policy" "audit" "Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy"; Teams policy changes audit log meeting policies administration activities Changed policy. Read ten cited pages and searched the Set reference for audit; no policy-setting audit event is named.

claims.claim: Meeting policies can be edited at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Edit.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies or Events policies.
Choose the policy by clicking to the left of the policy name, and then select Edit.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -<parameter> <value> updates a meeting policy using its named settings.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity SalesMeetingPolicy -AllowTranscription $True
The command shown in Example 1 uses the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet to update an existing meeting policy with the Identity SalesMeetingPolicy.

claims.claim: Group assignment is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Group policy assignment > Add.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
To groups: Go to the Group policy assignment tab, select Add, enter the group name, select the policy name, and then select Apply.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Group <group ID> -PolicyName <policy name> -Rank <rank> assigns a meeting policy to a group.
claims.quote: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Group d8ebfa45-0f28-4d2d-9bcc-b158a49e2d17 -PolicyName "Retail Managers Meeting Policy" -Rank 1

claims.claim: Individual assignment is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Manage users > Assign users.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
To specific users: Select your policy, select Manage users > Assign users, enter the names of specific users in the search bar, select Add, and then select Apply.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <user> -PolicyName <policy name> assigns a meeting policy to an individual user.
claims.quote: Grant-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity reda@contoso.com -PolicyName "Student Meeting Policy"

claims.claim: Recording is controlled at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting recording.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
Turn the Meeting recording toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowCloudRecording $true enables recording permission in that policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowCloudRecording $true

claims.claim: Transcription is controlled at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true enables transcription permission.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Live captions is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Live captions.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
From the drop-down for Live captions, select Not enabled, but users can enable(default value) or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled prevents live captions.
claims.quote:
To turn off live captions for users with this policy, run the following script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled

claims.claim: Copilot is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Copilot.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
Go to the Recording & transcription section and find the Copilot setting.

claims.quote: On | Enabled | When organizers with this policy create meetings and events, Copilot's default value in their meeting options is Only during the meeting.
